title: Frame cofibration pushout product with simplicial trivial cofibrations
statement: Use model categories, cofibrant objects, cosimplicial frames and their Reedy cofibrations as in [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] and [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and simplicial sets with their Kan–Quillen model structure (cofibrations the monomorphisms, weak homotopy equivalences, trivial cofibrations) as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with functorial factorizations, and let $A^\bullet$ and $B^\bullet$ be cosimplicial frames on cofibrant objects $A$ and $B$. Let $f:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ be a Reedy cofibration. For a simplicial set $K$, let $A^\bullet\otimes K=\operatorname{colim}_{(\Delta^n\to K)}A^n$ be the colimit of $A^\bullet$ over the category of simplices of $K$ (equivalently the coend $\int^{[r]\in\Delta}\coprod_{K_r}A^r$), functorial in $A^\bullet$ and $K$, with $A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^n\cong A^n$; by the universal property of colimits it satisfies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A^\bullet\otimes K,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,H(A^\bullet,Y))$, naturally in $A^\bullet$, $K$ and $Y$, where $H(A^\bullet,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A^n,Y)$. Define $B^\bullet\otimes K$ similarly. For every trivial cofibration $i:K\to L$ of simplicial sets, the induced pushout-product map $$(A^\bullet\otimes L)\amalg_{A^\bullet\otimes K}(B^\bullet\otimes K)\longrightarrow B^\bullet\otimes L$$ is a trivial cofibration in $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Hovey, Model categories, Proposition 5.4.3, printed pp.130-131 (PDF pp.139-140), first clause; the tensor $A^\bullet\otimes K$ and its adjunction are those of Proposition 3.1.5 (Section 3.1) and Remark 5.2.9.

proof.text: For $T^\bullet=A^\bullet$ or $B^\bullet$, write $V_T(K)=T^\bullet\otimes K$. The displayed tensor–Hom adjunction makes $V_T$ a left adjoint; explicitly, maps from $V_T(\operatorname{colim}_a K_a)$ to any $Y$ are compatible families of maps $K_a\to H(T^\bullet,Y)$, hence compatible families $V_T(K_a)\to Y$. Thus $V_T$ preserves all small colimits. There is a natural identification $V_T(\partial\Delta^n)=L_nT^\bullet$, compatible with the map to $V_T(\Delta^n)=T^n$: a map $\partial\Delta^n\to H(T^\bullet,Y)$ is a family $T^r\to Y$ indexed by the proper injective maps $[r]\hookrightarrow[n]$, agreeing under the triangles between such maps. Every other simplex of the boundary factors as a surjection followed by a proper injection, and its value is forced by that family. These are precisely the cocones defining $L_nT^\bullet$; the identification follows from the two universal properties. For $n=0$ both indexing data are empty and both objects are initial.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1, proof: boundary tensor identifies with the latching object; Proposition 3.1.5 for the adjunction.

proof.text:
Fix any trivial fibration $p:E\to F$ in $\mathcal M$, with no fibrancy assumption on $E$ or $F$. Form the simplicial corner map
$$q_p:H(B^\bullet,E)\longrightarrow H(A^\bullet,E)\times_{H(A^\bullet,F)}H(B^\bullet,F).$$
Apply the parametrized-adjunction corner-lifting equivalence to the tensor–Hom adjunction, with first arrow $f$, second arrow $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, and third arrow $p$. By Step 1 its left corner arrow is
$$\lambda_n f:A^n\amalg_{L_nA^\bullet}L_nB^\bullet\longrightarrow B^n.$$
The Reedy cofibration hypothesis says exactly that $\lambda_n f$ is a cofibration. The ground model-category lifting axiom gives $\lambda_n f\perp p$. The corner-lifting equivalence therefore says that $q_p$ lifts every boundary inclusion, including $n=0$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1: relative latching cofibration argument, expressed through tensor–Hom corner lifting.

proof.text: The Kan–Quillen characterization of trivial fibrations by boundary lifting makes $q_p$ a trivial fibration of simplicial sets. Since the given $i:K\to L$ is a cofibration there, the Kan–Quillen lifting axiom gives $i\perp q_p$. Apply the same parametrized-adjunction corner-lifting equivalence, now with second arrow $i$. It gives $(f\mathbin\square i)\perp p$. This holds for every trivial fibration $p$ in $\mathcal M$, so the weak factorization system $(C,F\cap W)$ of the ground model category implies that $f\mathbin\square i$ is a cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1, cofibration conclusion; model-category lifting characterization.

proof.text: For each of the two frames $T^\bullet$, Step 1 identifies $V_T(\partial\Delta^n)\to V_T(\Delta^n)$ with its cofibration $L_nT^\bullet\to T^n$. Also the collapse $V_T(\Delta^n)\to V_T(\Delta^0)$ identifies with $T^n\to T^0$. This is the augmentation component: naturality of the augmentation for $[n]\to[0]$ and its identity component in degree zero give precisely that equality. It is therefore a weak equivalence by the definition of a frame. The boundary-and-collapse test applies to the colimit-preserving $V_T$ of Step 1, and shows that $V_T(i)$ is a trivial cofibration. Consequently both $A^\bullet\otimes K\to A^\bullet\otimes L$ and $B^\bullet\otimes K\to B^\bullet\otimes L$ are trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.3, proof using Proposition 3.6.8 and the frame augmentation.

proof.text: Let $P=(A^\bullet\otimes L)\amalg_{A^\bullet\otimes K}(B^\bullet\otimes K)$ and $h=f\mathbin\square i:P\to B^\bullet\otimes L$. The map $j:B^\bullet\otimes K\to P$ is the pushout of $A^\bullet\otimes i$. Trivial cofibrations are the left lifting class of all fibrations, so their pushout closure gives that $j$ is a trivial cofibration. By the defining pushout maps, $hj=B^\bullet\otimes i$, which is a weak equivalence by Step 4; $j$ is also a weak equivalence. Two-out-of-three gives that $h$ is a weak equivalence. Step 3 already gives that $h$ is a cofibration, so $h$ is a trivial cofibration, as required.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.3, final pushout and two-out-of-three argument.

proof_origin.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Propositions 5.4.1 and 5.4.3, printed pp.130–131 (PDF pp.139–140), and Proposition 3.6.8. Read online; not archived in literature/. Cofibration reduction is written using the existing parametrized-adjunction lifting node instead of a new generator-extension lemma.
